Sets one question, fixes a time box in days (or one week), a maximum cost per correct answer derived from the handler minutes it replaces, a target and stop line per class (stricter on bodily injury, which gets more cases, sized for its stop line) and a kill date before building; starts with a fixed workflow, not an agent; anonymised or synthetic cases only; removes forwarding in code (the lethal-trifecta check); ends on go to PRD, reshape or stop.

Reads each class with its Wilson interval (passports about 79% to 98%, registry extracts about 60% to 98%), says neither demonstrates 90% and that 9 of 10 falls under the 75% stop line at its lower bound, so registry extracts are undecided; goes to PRD for passports only with the class flagged as not demonstrated, reshapes registry extracts (more cases under a new appetite, or out of scope), and names the size build-evals needs.
